title: ₹10 Lakh Ki Car Bikti Hai, Dealer Ko Kitna Milta Hai?
description: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. Owning a car showroom is an aspirational dream, but nobody knows the economics. The surprise that the car is not the profit centre gives a strong hook and a reason to share. Dealer margin ranges are published in company filings and auto-industry reports.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: CAR DEALERSHIP ECONOMICS IN INDIA
Compiled 3 Nov 2026. Where a source is old or an estimate, the bullet says so.

SCRIPT WARNING (READ FIRST)
- No source supports "a few thousand rupees" on a ₹10 lakh car. The sourced figure is a gross margin of about ₹50,000 on a ₹10 lakh car at 5%. This is an illustrative example, not a measured dealer figure. [https://cfosme.in/automotive-dealership-financial-kpis-2025/]
- Landmark Cars, a listed dealer, reported a new-car segment margin of 2.0% in Q4 FY26. [https://www.mnclgroup.com/landmark-cars-q4fy26-company-update]
- Suggested hook: "₹50,000 on paper, ~2% in reality." This is a framing suggestion; check the exact wording against the sources.
- Landmark is mostly a premium and luxury dealer (Honda, MG, BYD, Mercedes). It is not a typical Maruti or Hyundai dealer. Say so on screen.

1. DEALER MARGIN PER NEW CAR (FIXED OEM MARGIN)
- Most OEMs give under 5% average fixed dealer margin. Maruti is at 5.07% and MG at 5.22%. [https://www.rushlane.com/car-dealer-margins-india-fada-survey-12364355.html]
- Hyundai is 4.38%, Tata 3.74%, Honda 3.41%, Mahindra 3.75%, Toyota 2.32% and Kia 4.43%. [https://www.rushlane.com/car-dealer-margins-india-fada-survey-12364355.html]
- This FADA survey is from about 2020, so the numbers are dated. Ask FADA or a dealer for a current figure.
- In the under-₹4 lakh segment, Maruti gave dealers 5.58% to 6.05% and Renault 4.32% to 4.33%. [https://www.thehitavada.com/Encyc/2020/6/9/Auto-dealers-fixed-margin-in-India-low-FADA.html]
- In the ₹4–6 lakh band, Maruti's margins were 2.9% to 5.68% and Hyundai's 4.22% to 5.57%. [https://www.thehitavada.com/Encyc/2020/6/9/Auto-dealers-fixed-margin-in-India-low-FADA.html]
- FADA wrote to SIAM asking for the fixed margin to go up to 7% of selling price. [https://www.thehitavada.com/Encyc/2020/6/9/Auto-dealers-fixed-margin-in-India-low-FADA.html]
- Comparison, per FADA: US 8–10%, China 9–11%, France/Germany/Italy 13–14%, UK 6–8%. [https://www.thehitavada.com/Encyc/2020/6/9/Auto-dealers-fixed-margin-in-India-low-FADA.html]
- A 2025 explainer gives a range of 2.9% to 7.5% of ex-showroom price, depending on brand and segment. [https://cfosme.in/automotive-dealership-financial-kpis-2025/]
- A Delhi Maruti dealer said a NEXA outlet selling 150–200 cars a month earns over 6% margin, against 4–5% otherwise. [https://www.outlookbusiness.com/amp/story/strategy/feature/keeping-the-flock-happy-2872] This is a dealer quote from an older article.
- FADA's Dealer Satisfaction Study 2026 says profitability, inventory management and long-term viability remain key concerns. [https://www.rushlane.com/indias-largest-auto-brands-arent-no-1-in-dealer-satisfaction-fada-study-12554950.html]
- The study is based on 2,045 dealer responses collected in July–August 2026. [https://www.autopunditz.com/post/fada-dealer-satisfaction-study-2026-jsw-mg-royal-enfield-tata-motors]
- "Profitability and margins" was the most frequent improvement request from dealers. [https://www.drivespark.com/four-wheelers/2026/fada-dealer-satisfaction-study-2026-jsw-mg-royal-enfield-lead-088109.html]

2. WHERE THE REAL PROFIT COMES FROM

SERVICE (the biggest profit source)
- Marcellus estimate (not audited): service is about a fifth of a car dealer's revenue but about 70% of its operating profit. [https://marcellus.in/blogs/new-kings-queens-indias-auto-dealers/]
- Service earns 37% ROCE against 9% for the dealership overall. [https://marcellus.in/blogs/new-kings-queens-indias-auto-dealers/]
- Landmark Cars FY26 after-sales: 41.2% gross margin, 18.1% EBITDA margin and 29.8% RoCE. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/landmark-q1fy27-97835]
- FY26 after-sales revenue was ₹1,051 crore, crossing ₹1,000 crore for the first time. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/landmark-fy26-95044]
- After-sales EBITDA for FY26 was ₹191 crore. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/landmark-fy26-95044]
- Q4 FY26 after-sales service margin was 20.1%, the best ever reported by the company. [https://www.mnclgroup.com/landmark-cars-q4fy26-company-update]
- Landmark's executive director said car-sales margin is only about 6–8% (gross). He said service gives about 40% gross margin and 18% EBITDA margin. [https://www.cartoq.com/car-life/top-car-dealer-reveals-profit-margins-car-retail-business/]
- He also said service is usually as capital-intensive as sales. [https://www.cartoq.com/car-life/top-car-dealer-reveals-profit-margins-car-retail-business/]

INSURANCE COMMISSION (the "I never knew that" fact)
- Motor dealers and OEM-linked brokers earned almost ₹7,050 crore in commission on ₹29,000 crore of premium in FY25, per IRDAI. [https://upstox.com/news/personal-finance/insurance/buying-a-new-car-your-dealer-may-earn-up-to-38-commission-on-motor-insurance-irdai-moves-to-rein-it-in/article-200834/]
- Motor dealers selling insurance as MISPs average a 38% commission on new vehicles. [https://upstox.com/news/personal-finance/insurance/buying-a-new-car-your-dealer-may-earn-up-to-38-commission-on-motor-insurance-irdai-moves-to-rein-it-in/article-200834/]
- OEM brokers average 27% on new-vehicle policies. [https://retailintel.in/signal/irdai-proposes-nil-third-party-commission-on-new-car-policie-d995d961]
- Motor insurance averages 24% commission across all channels, with a range of 13% to 50%. [https://upstox.com/news/personal-finance/insurance/buying-a-new-car-your-dealer-may-earn-up-to-38-commission-on-motor-insurance-irdai-moves-to-rein-it-in/article-200834/]
- This is true "even though a significant part of the premium is mandatory third-party cover on regulated tariffs." [https://upstox.com/news/personal-finance/insurance/buying-a-new-car-your-dealer-may-earn-up-to-38-commission-on-motor-insurance-irdai-moves-to-rein-it-in/article-200834/]
- Between FY23 and FY25, motor premiums grew about 34% while dealer and broker commissions jumped nearly 259%. [https://thepamphlet.in/irdais-new-commission-rules-aim-to-make-insurance-fairer-for-customers/]
- IRDAI noted that "mostly, the choice of motor insurance policy is guided by the motor vehicle dealer" and not by the customer. [https://upstox.com/news/personal-finance/insurance/buying-a-new-car-your-dealer-may-earn-up-to-38-commission-on-motor-insurance-irdai-moves-to-rein-it-in/article-200834/]
- PROPOSED RULE, NOT FINAL: IRDAI's consultation paper of 23 Sep 2026 proposes nil commission on new-car third-party cover for distribution entities. [https://www.coverfox.com/news/irdai-proposes-changes-to-insurance-commissions-and-expense-limits/]
